a stud on a rack has been sold and handled this many times:
1. timber broker        sells the standing timber
2. logging contractor   fells and skids it
3. log haulier          trucks it to the mill yard
4. log scaler           measures and grades the log
5. headrig sawyer       breaks the log down
6. edger operator       squares the waney sides
8. kiln operator        dries it to a moisture spec
9. lumber grader        stamps a grade on it
10. planing mill         surfaces four sides to dimension
11. bundler              packs and wraps a unit
14. distributor          holds stock and breaks bulk
15. retail yard          sells you one stick
then sales tax: $8.88 on the rack becomes $10.00 paid
every one of the 15 took a margin, and every margin is in that price
the wedge path is: fell the tree, rip the trunk, use the wood

turn it about its own long axis and the SHAPE stays the same
while the STIFFNESS does not, because bending in a shell is
